newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican authorities search home in Salinas case.
newsitem.headline: Mexican authorities search home in Salinas case.

text.p: Mexican authorities searched a luxury home in southern Mexico City on Monday in pursuit of evidence against the brother of a former president jailed on murder and illegal enrichment charges, officials said.
The search was the latest twist in the case against Raul Salinas de Gortari, the brother of disgraced former President Carlos Salinas de Gortari.
Raul Salinas is in a maximum-security prison on charges of murder and illegal enrichment while his brother, the former president, lives in Ireland in self-imposed exile.

The Attorney General's Office (PGR) said in a news release that "objects and documents" related to the illegal enrichment case were found in the house, which belongs to the son of another former president, the late Gustavo Diaz Ordaz.
The private Television Azteca network reported in its nightly newscast that Raul Salinas' former mistress tipped off authorities that important records might be found in the house.
Video clips from the news programme showed Salinas' wife, Paula Castanon, arriving at the scene and being allowed past guards at the front gate, but Salinas' lawyer, Javier Olea, was not allowed in.
Castanon was married to the owner of the house, Alfredo Diaz Ordaz Borja, before Raul Salinas, the PGR said.
"It's absurd and moreover totally in violation of the constitution because they didn't even let me in," Olea told Television Azteca.
Olea warned that authorities might plant evidence on the scene, saying, "As you all know, there is always the possibility with so many people in a such a big operation."
Authorities have planted evidence against Salinas in the past, leading to the arrest of a former special prosecutor accused of having a body buried on a ranch used by Salinas.

Raul Salinas was arrested in 1995, shortly after his brother's six-year term ended, and charged with arranging the 1994 murder of Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu, the number two leader of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI).
In the wake of his arrest, authorities found millions of dollars stashed in Swiss bank accounts controlled by Salinas, who was a high-level bureaucrat in his brother's government.
Carlos Salinas fled the country soon thereafter.
